tweets.title: Trump’s demands stretch US Navy to its limits The US Navy is facing mounting pressure as Trump pushes an ambitious fleet expansion while existing forces remain stretched by prolonged deployments, shipbuilding delays and rising costs. The USS Abraham Lincoln spent a record 260 days at sea without a port visit, surpassing the previous 204-day record. Sailors and families have raised concerns over exhaustion and mental health. At the same time, Trump’s proposed “Golden Fleet” includes nuclear-powered battleships potentially costing over $23 billion each, while US shipyards are already struggling with backlogs involving carriers, submarines and destroyers. The administration is also reviewing a return to steam-powered catapults on Ford-class carriers, potentially disrupting the electromagnetic launch systems already being developed.
tweets.content:

At the same time, Trump’s proposed “Golden Fleet” includes nuclear-powered battleships potentially costing over $23 billion each, while US shipyards are already struggling with backlogs involving carriers, submarines and destroyers.
